===== FILE: scripts/dev/apply_step62_nudge_repeat.py =====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Step 62: repeat the continuation nudge up to 3 times until the
Executor checks in.

Step 60 introduced a one-shot [CONTINUATION] hint: fires once on the
first Executor step if plan.md was present at task start. Live ASDI
runs showed this is not enough — sometimes the Executor acknowledges
immediately, sometimes it silently starts work. In the second case a
single hint is easy to miss.

This step fires the nudge on every Executor step while:
  - hasPlanAtStart is true,
  - the Executor has not yet sent any message to the Critic,
  - and fewer than MAX_CONTINUATION_NUDGES attempts have been used.

Satisfaction is set on the first successful send_message from the
Executor, regardless of what the message says (any talk counts as a
check-in). After satisfaction, the nudge never fires again this run.

MAX_CONTINUATION_NUDGES = 3: enough to catch the Executor's
attention, few enough not to dominate the prompt. No change to
checkpoint_nudge (fires at 15 executes, independent).

Run from the pingis/ extension root:
    python scripts/dev/apply_step62_nudge_repeat.py
"""

import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
BACKUP = ROOT / ".backup" / "dev-snapshot-v32"


def backup(rel: str) -> None:
    src = ROOT / rel
    if not src.exists():
        return
    dst = BACKUP / rel
    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copy2(src, dst)


def patch(rel: str, pairs: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> int:
    p = ROOT / rel
    if not p.exists():
        print(f"  ✗ {rel}: not found")
        return -1
    text = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    original = text
    total = 0
    for old, new in pairs:
        if old == new:
            continue
        if new in text and old not in text:
            print(f"  = {rel}: already patched")
            continue
        if new in text and old in text:
            print(f"  ✗ {rel}: both old and new present — file drifted")
            return -1
        n = text.count(old)
        if n == 0:
            print(f"  ✗ {rel}: pattern not found; expected:")
            print(f"    {old[:200]!r}")
            return -1
        if n > 1:
            print(f"  ✗ {rel}: pattern appears {n} times; aborting")
            return -1
        text = text.replace(old, new)
        total += n
        print(f"  + {rel}: {n} occurrence(s)")
    if text != original:
        backup(rel)
        p.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    return total


def write_new(rel: str, content: str) -> None:
    p = ROOT / rel
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if p.exists():
        backup(rel)
    p.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"  + {rel} (new, {len(content)} bytes)")


def run_cmd(cmd: list[str], label: str) -> bool:
    print()
    print(f"=== {label} ===")
    print("$ " + " ".join(cmd))
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=ROOT)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print(f"  ✗ {label} failed (exit {r.returncode})")
        return False
    print(f"  + {label} ok")
    return True


def git_commit(message: str) -> None:
    if not (ROOT / ".git").exists():
        print("  git: no repo, skipping commit")
        return
    try:
        subprocess.run(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=ROOT,
                       check=True, capture_output=True)
        subprocess.run(["git", "commit", "-m", message], cwd=ROOT,
                       check=True, capture_output=True)
        print(f"  git: committed \"{message}\"")
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
        print(f"  git: commit failed ({e})")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# src/orchestrator.ts
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1) New constant.
CONST_OLD = """const CHECKPOINT_NUDGE_AFTER = 15;"""

CONST_NEW = """const CHECKPOINT_NUDGE_AFTER = 15;

/**
 * Maximum number of [CONTINUATION] hints the orchestrator sends to
 * the Executor in a single run when plan.md was present at start.
 * Fires on each Executor step until the Executor sends any message
 * to the Critic, or until this cap is reached.
 */
const MAX_CONTINUATION_NUDGES = 3;"""


# 2) Fields.
FIELDS_OLD = """  // Snapshot of plan.md existence at the moment run() started.
  // Used by step() to inject the one-shot [CONTINUATION] hint.
  private hasPlanAtStart = false;

  // One-shot guard: true once the continuation nudge has been sent
  // to the Executor in this run. Prevents repeated hints if the
  // Executor chooses to ignore the first one.
  private continuationNudged = false;"""

FIELDS_NEW = """  // Snapshot of plan.md existence at the moment run() started.
  // Used by step() to inject the [CONTINUATION] hint.
  private hasPlanAtStart = false;

  // Continuation nudge: fires on Executor steps while plan.md was
  // present at start and the Executor has not yet sent any message
  // to the Critic. Capped at MAX_CONTINUATION_NUDGES attempts per
  // run. Live runs showed the Executor sometimes responds to the
  // first hint, sometimes silently starts work; repeating helps in
  // the second case without dominating the prompt.
  private continuationNudgeCount = 0;
  private continuationNudgeSatisfied = false;"""


# 3) Step block.
STEP_OLD = """    // One-shot continuation nudge: if this run started with a plan
    // present, remind the Executor on its first request to actually
    // consult that plan and send RESUME:. Real runs showed Executor
    // silently ignoring the protocol. We do not enforce; we hint.
    if (who === 'executor'
        && this.hasPlanAtStart
        && !this.continuationNudged) {
      this.continuationNudged = true;
      this.log.event(who, 'continuation_nudge', {});
      msgForCall = {
        role: 'user',
        content:
          '[CONTINUATION] .pingis/plan.md exists from a prior run.\\n\\n' +
          'First action: read that file, find the first unchecked ' +
          'item (- [ ]), and send the Critic:\\n\\n' +
          '    RESUME: continuing from stage N/M.\\n' +
          '    Already done: <brief>. Continuing with <stage name>.\\n\\n' +
          'Wait for APPROVE_PLAN before continuing work.\\n\\n' +
          '---\\n\\n' +
          msgForCall.content
      };
    }"""

STEP_NEW = """    // Continuation nudge: while the Executor has not yet sent any
    // message to the Critic, remind it on each step to read plan.md
    // and send RESUME:. Real runs showed the Executor sometimes
    // ignores the protocol and silently starts work; a single
    // one-shot hint was too easy to miss. Fires up to
    // MAX_CONTINUATION_NUDGES times, then stops.
    if (who === 'executor'
        && this.hasPlanAtStart
        && !this.continuationNudgeSatisfied
        && this.continuationNudgeCount < MAX_CONTINUATION_NUDGES) {
      this.continuationNudgeCount++;
      this.log.event(who, 'continuation_nudge', {
        attempt: this.continuationNudgeCount,
        max: MAX_CONTINUATION_NUDGES
      });
      msgForCall = {
        role: 'user',
        content:
          '[CONTINUATION] .pingis/plan.md exists from a prior run.\\n\\n' +
          'First action: read that file, find the first stage not ' +
          'marked [x], and send the Critic:\\n\\n' +
          '    RESUME: continuing from stage N/M.\\n' +
          '    Already done: <brief>. Continuing with <stage name>.\\n\\n' +
          'Wait for APPROVE_PLAN before continuing work.\\n\\n' +
          '---\\n\\n' +
          msgForCall.content
      };
    }"""


# 4) handleToolCall send_message — satisfy.
SEND_OLD = """    if (tc.name === 'send_message') {
      // Any send_message counts as a check-in: reset the execute
      // streak for this agent.
      if (who === 'executor') this.executeStreakE = 0;
      else this.executeStreakC = 0;"""

SEND_NEW = """    if (tc.name === 'send_message') {
      // Any send_message counts as a check-in: reset the execute
      // streak for this agent, and (for the Executor) mark the
      // continuation nudge as satisfied — no more [CONTINUATION]
      // hints this run.
      if (who === 'executor') {
        this.executeStreakE = 0;
        this.continuationNudgeSatisfied = true;
      } else {
        this.executeStreakC = 0;
      }"""

LOG_OLD = """    case 'continuation_nudge':
      return 'plan.md present; injected RESUME hint';"""

LOG_NEW = """    case 'continuation_nudge':
      return `attempt ${r.attempt}/${r.max}; plan.md RESUME hint`;"""

CHANGELOG_NEW = """## [Unreleased]

### Changed

- **Continuation nudge now repeats up to 3 times.** If the Executor
  ignores the first `[CONTINUATION]` hint and starts work without

  next Executor step, up to `MAX_CONTINUATION_NUDGES = 3`. It stops

PROBE_NUDGE = r'''/**

 * T1. plan.md present, Executor sends RESUME on its first response.
 *     Nudge fires exactly once. Second Executor step has no prefix.
 * T2. plan.md present, Executor ignores the hint and does five

import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as os from 'os';
import * as path from 'path';
import { ApiClient } from '../src/api';
import { Executor } from '../src/executor';
import { Logger } from '../src/log';
import { NullPanel, Orchestrator } from '../src/orchestrator';
import { AssistantResponse, ExecResult } from '../src/types';

let failures = 0;

function check(condition: boolean, label: string): void {
  if (condition) {
    console.log(`  ✓ ${label}`);
  } else {
    console.error(`  ✗ ${label}`);
    failures++;
  }
}

function freshTmp(name: string): string {
  const p = path.join(os.tmpdir(),
    `${name}-${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8)}`);
  fs.mkdirSync(p, { recursive: true });
  return p;
}

type Step =
  | { kind: 'execute' }
  | { kind: 'tools'; calls: { name: string; args: any }[] };

class FakeApi {
  public receivedContents: string[] = [];
  constructor(private who: string, private script: Step[]) {}
  private idx = 0;
  async newChat(): Promise<void> { /* no-op */ }
  async chat(_session: unknown, msg: { content: string }): Promise<AssistantResponse> {
    this.receivedContents.push(msg.content);
    if (this.idx >= this.script.length) {
      throw new Error(`FakeApi(${this.who}): script exhausted`);
    }
    const s = this.script[this.idx++];
    if (s.kind === 'execute') {
      return {
        text: '',
        tool_calls: [{
          id: `call_${this.idx}`,
          name: 'execute',
          args: { script: 'print(1)' }
        } as any],
        raw: {}
      };
    }
    return {
      text: '',
      tool_calls: s.calls.map((c, i) => ({
        id: `call_${this.idx}_${i}`,
        name: c.name as any,
        args: c.args
      })) as any,
      raw: {}
    };
  }
}

class FakeExecutor {
  async run(call_id: string, script: string): Promise<ExecResult> {
    return {
      call_id, command: 'noop', exit_code: 0, duration_ms: 1,
      stdout: 'ok\n', stderr: '',
      stdout_truncated: false, stderr_truncated: false
    };
  }
}

function mkLog(cwd: string): Logger {
  return new Logger(cwd, { appendLine: () => { /* silent */ } });
}

async function runOrch(
  cwd: string,
  apiE: FakeApi,
  apiC: FakeApi
): Promise<void> {
  const log = mkLog(cwd);
  const orch = new Orchestrator(
    apiE as unknown as ApiClient,
    apiC as unknown as ApiClient,
    new FakeExecutor() as unknown as Executor,
    new NullPanel(),
    log,
    {
      cwd, name: 'probe-continuation-nudge', task: 'stub',
      deadlineAt: Date.now() + 60_000,
      executorPrompt: 'E', criticPrompt: 'C'
    }
  );
  await orch.run();
  log.close();
  await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 200));
}

function readLog(cwd: string): any[] {
  const logPath = path.join(cwd, '.pingis', 'session.log');
  if (!fs.existsSync(logPath)) return [];
  return fs.readFileSync(logPath, 'utf-8')
    .split('\n').filter(Boolean).map(l => JSON.parse(l));
}

async function t1_stops_after_first_check_in(): Promise<void> {
  console.log('\nT1: Executor sends RESUME first → 1 nudge');

  const cwd = freshTmp('probe-cont-t1');
  fs.mkdirSync(path.join(cwd, '.pingis'), { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(cwd, '.pingis', 'plan.md'),
    '# Plan\n- [ ] 5. do a thing\n');

  const apiE = new FakeApi('executor', [
    { kind: 'tools',
      calls: [{ name: 'send_message',
                args: { to: 'critic',
                        message: 'RESUME: continuing from stage 5.' } }] },
    { kind: 'tools',
      calls: [{ name: 'send_message',
                args: { to: 'critic', message: 'ALL DONE: ok' } }] }
  ]);
  const apiC = new FakeApi('critic', [
    { kind: 'tools',
      calls: [{ name: 'send_message',
                args: { to: 'executor', message: 'APPROVE_PLAN' } }] },
    { kind: 'tools',
      calls: [{ name: 'finalize', args: { comment: 'done' } }] }
  ]);

  await runOrch(cwd, apiE, apiC);
  const lines = readLog(cwd);

  const nudges = lines.filter(e => e.event === 'continuation_nudge');
  check(nudges.length === 1,
    `exactly one continuation_nudge (got ${nudges.length})`);
  if (nudges.length === 1) {
    check(nudges[0].attempt === 1,
      `attempt = ${nudges[0].attempt} (expected 1)`);
  }

  const prefixed = apiE.receivedContents.filter(
    c => c.startsWith('[CONTINUATION]')
  );
  check(prefixed.length === 1,
    `exactly one executor request has [CONTINUATION] (got ${prefixed.length})`);
  if (apiE.receivedContents.length >= 2) {
    check(!apiE.receivedContents[1].startsWith('[CONTINUATION]'),
      'second executor request has no prefix');
  }
}

  console.log('\nT2: Executor ignores hint → 3 nudges, then stops');

  const apiE = new FakeApi('executor', [
    { kind: 'execute' },
    { kind: 'execute' },
    { kind: 'execute' },
    { kind: 'execute' },
    { kind: 'execute' },
    { kind: 'tools',
      calls: [{ name: 'send_message',
                args: { to: 'critic', message: 'ALL DONE: ok' } }] }

  const apiC = new FakeApi('critic', [
    { kind: 'tools',
      calls: [{ name: 'finalize', args: { comment: 'done' } }] }
  ]);

  await runOrch(cwd, apiE, apiC);
  const lines = readLog(cwd);

    check(attempts[0] === 1 && attempts[1] === 2 && attempts[2] === 3,

async function t3_no_plan_no_nudge(): Promise<void> {
  console.log('\nT3: plan.md absent → no nudge');

===== FILE: scripts/dev/apply_step63_network_no_restart.py =====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Step 63: do not restart agents on network_error retry.

Live ASDI run showed the retry loop hanging for minutes after a
transient ECONNRESET. Root cause: onRetry unconditionally restarts
the API agents (stop-all.sh + start-all.sh + waitBothReady, 30-60s)
for any retryable reason. For network_error the agents are healthy —
the link between the extension host and the API blipped. Restarting
is expensive and, if the network is still flaky, may itself hang.

Fix: add shouldRestartAgentsOnRetry(reason) in retry.ts. Returns
true only for server_error / bad_gateway (API process is in a bad
state, restart helps). Returns false for network_error — the loop
just waits the backoff and retries with the same agents.

Run from the pingis/ extension root:
    python scripts/dev/apply_step63_network_no_restart.py
"""

import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
BACKUP = ROOT / ".backup" / "dev-snapshot-v33"


def backup(rel: str) -> None:
    src = ROOT / rel
    if not src.exists():
        return
    dst = BACKUP / rel
    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copy2(src, dst)


def patch(rel: str, pairs: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> int:
    p = ROOT / rel
    if not p.exists():
        print(f"  ✗ {rel}: not found")
        return -1
    text = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    original = text
    total = 0
    for old, new in pairs:
        if old == new:
            continue
        if new in text and old not in text:
            print(f"  = {rel}: already patched")
            continue
        if new in text and old in text:
            print(f"  ✗ {rel}: both old and new present — file drifted")
            return -1
        n = text.count(old)
        if n == 0:
            print(f"  ✗ {rel}: pattern not found; expected:")
            print(f"    {old[:200]!r}")
            return -1
        if n > 1:
            print(f"  ✗ {rel}: pattern appears {n} times; aborting")
            return -1
        text = text.replace(old, new)
        total += n
        print(f"  + {rel}: {n} occurrence(s)")
    if text != original:
        backup(rel)
        p.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    return total


def write_new(rel: str, content: str) -> None:
    p = ROOT / rel
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if p.exists():
        backup(rel)
    p.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"  + {rel} (new, {len(content)} bytes)")


def run_cmd(cmd: list[str], label: str) -> bool:
    print()
    print(f"=== {label} ===")
    print("$ " + " ".join(cmd))
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=ROOT)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print(f"  ✗ {label} failed (exit {r.returncode})")
        return False
    print(f"  + {label} ok")
    return True


def git_commit(message: str) -> None:
    if not (ROOT / ".git").exists():
        print("  git: no repo, skipping commit")
        return
    try:
        subprocess.run(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=ROOT,
                       check=True, capture_output=True)
        subprocess.run(["git", "commit", "-m", message], cwd=ROOT,
                       check=True, capture_output=True)
        print(f"  git: committed \"{message}\"")
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
        print(f"  git: commit failed ({e})")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# src/retry.ts — new helper
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

RETRY_IMPORT_OLD = """import { OrchestratorResult, StopReason } from './types';"""

RETRY_IMPORT_NEW = """import { OrchestratorResult, StopReason } from './types';

/**
 * Decide whether a retry attempt should restart the API agents.
 *
 *   server_error / bad_gateway — the API process itself is unhealthy.
 *     Restarting clears state and gives a fresh Chromium.
 *
 *   network_error — the connection between the extension host and the
 *     API dropped mid-request. The agents are usually healthy; a
 *     restart costs 30-60s and, if the underlying network is still
 *     flaky, may itself hang waiting for Chromium init. Skip the
 *     restart, let the backoff sleep and the next attempt decide.
 */
export function shouldRestartAgentsOnRetry(reason: StopReason): boolean {
  return reason === 'server_error' || reason === 'bad_gateway';
}"""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# src/panel.ts — use the helper
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

PANEL_IMPORT_OLD = """import { runWithRetry } from './retry';"""

PANEL_IMPORT_NEW = """import { runWithRetry, shouldRestartAgentsOnRetry } from './retry';"""


PANEL_ONRETRY_OLD = """      onRetry: async (attempt, max) => {
        this.post({ type: 'retrying', attempt, max });
        this.agents?.stop();
        this.agents = new AgentsProcess(apiDir, this.log!);
        await this.agents.ensureRunning();
      }"""

PANEL_ONRETRY_NEW = """      onRetry: async (attempt, max, reason) => {
        this.post({ type: 'retrying', attempt, max });
        if (shouldRestartAgentsOnRetry(reason)) {
          this.agents?.stop();
          this.agents = new AgentsProcess(apiDir, this.log!);
          await this.agents.ensureRunning();
        } else {
          // network_error (and anything else not covered by the
          // helper): agents are fine, just wait the backoff. This
          // avoids a 30-60s Chromium restart on every transient
          // network blip.
          this.log?.event('orchestrator', 'retry', {
            __phase: 'skip_agent_restart',
            reason
          });
        }
      }"""

CHANGELOG_NEW = """## [Unreleased]

### Fixed

- **No agent restart on `network_error` retry.** A transient
  `ECONNRESET` between the extension host and the API used to trigger
  a full stop-all + start-all cycle (30-60s per retry), which could
  hang for minutes if the network was still flaky. Restart is now
  reserved for `server_error` / `bad_gateway`, where the API process
  is actually unhealthy. For `network_error` the retry loop waits
  the backoff and retries with the same agents."""

===== FILE: scripts/dev/apply_step64_stop_aborts_retry.py =====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Step 64: user Stop must abort the retry loop.

Live ASDI run exposed this: after Orchestrator returned network_error,
runWithRetry entered its retry loop. The user clicked Stop. Nothing
happened — the button only stops the current Orchestrator, which was
already gone. The retry loop kept running: slept 5s, called onRetry,
which restarted the agents (up to 240s waiting for readiness), then
would have retried. The UI appeared frozen.

Fix:
  - PanelProvider owns an AbortController created at the start of each
    runWithRetry and cleared in a finally block.
  - The 'stop' webview message triggers both orchestrator.stop() and
    abortController.abort().
  - runWithRetry accepts an optional AbortSignal; when it fires, the
    loop exits before the next runOnce and before/after the backoff
    sleep. sleep is abort-aware so Stop is immediate, not deferred by
    up to 20s of backoff.
  - After runWithRetry returns, Panel checks signal.aborted: if true,
    it reports user_stopped instead of the underlying reason.

Known limitation: if the user clicks Stop *while* onRetry is already
running the agent restart, that restart is not interrupted mid-flight
(no signal plumbing into the deployment scripts). Worst case: one
restart completes, then the loop notices the abort and exits.

The old, now-unused `sleep()` helper at the end of retry.ts is left
in place. tsconfig has noUnusedLocals: false, so the compiler does not
complain. Cleanup is a separate concern.

Run from the pingis/ extension root:
    python scripts/dev/apply_step64_stop_aborts_retry.py
"""

import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
BACKUP = ROOT / ".backup" / "dev-snapshot-v34"


def backup(rel: str) -> None:
    src = ROOT / rel
    if not src.exists():
        return
    dst = BACKUP / rel
    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copy2(src, dst)


def patch(rel: str, pairs: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> int:
    p = ROOT / rel
    if not p.exists():
        print(f"  ✗ {rel}: not found")
        return -1
    text = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    original = text
    total = 0
    for old, new in pairs:
        if old == new:
            continue
        # Empty `new` means deletion. Handle it separately: the
        # `new in text` check is always true for "", which would
        # otherwise trip the "both present" safety below.
        if new == "":
            n = text.count(old)
            if n == 0:
                print(f"  = {rel}: already deleted")
                continue
            if n > 1:
                print(f"  ✗ {rel}: pattern appears {n} times; aborting")
                return -1
            text = text.replace(old, "")
            total += n
            print(f"  + {rel}: deleted ({n})")
            continue
        if new in text and old not in text:
            print(f"  = {rel}: already patched")
            continue
        if new in text and old in text:
            print(f"  ✗ {rel}: both old and new present — file drifted")
            return -1
        n = text.count(old)
        if n == 0:
            print(f"  ✗ {rel}: pattern not found; expected:")
            print(f"    {old[:200]!r}")
            return -1
        if n > 1:
            print(f"  ✗ {rel}: pattern appears {n} times; aborting")
            return -1
        text = text.replace(old, new)
        total += n
        print(f"  + {rel}: {n} occurrence(s)")
    if text != original:
        backup(rel)
        p.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    return total


def run_cmd(cmd: list[str], label: str) -> bool:
    print()
    print(f"=== {label} ===")
    print("$ " + " ".join(cmd))
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=ROOT)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print(f"  ✗ {label} failed (exit {r.returncode})")
        return False
    print(f"  + {label} ok")
    return True


def git_commit(message: str) -> None:
    if not (ROOT / ".git").exists():
        print("  git: no repo, skipping commit")
        return
    try:
        subprocess.run(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=ROOT,
                       check=True, capture_output=True)
        subprocess.run(["git", "commit", "-m", message], cwd=ROOT,
                       check=True, capture_output=True)
        print(f"  git: committed \"{message}\"")
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
        print(f"  git: commit failed ({e})")

# src/retry.ts

IMPORT_OLD = """import { OrchestratorResult, StopReason } from './types';"""

IMPORT_NEW = """import { OrchestratorResult, StopReason } from './types';

/**
 * Abort-aware sleep. Resolves when either the timer expires or the
 * signal fires. Used for backoff between retry attempts so a user
 * Stop is not delayed by up to 20s of pending backoff.
 */
function sleepWithAbort(ms: number, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<void> {
  if (!signal) {
    return new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, ms));
  }
  if (signal.aborted) return Promise.resolve();

  return new Promise(resolve => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      signal.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort);
      resolve();
    }, ms);
    const onAbort = () => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      resolve();
    };
    signal.addEventListener('abort', onAbort, { once: true });
  });
}"""


OPTS_OLD = """  log: (event: string, payload: object) => void;
}"""

OPTS_NEW = """  log: (event: string, payload: object) => void;

  /**
   * Optional abort signal. When it fires, the retry loop exits
   * before the next runOnce and at the start/end of the backoff
   * sleep. Used to make the UI Stop button actually stop the loop —
   * previously it could only stop the current Orchestrator, which is
   * already gone by the time a retry is scheduled.
   */
  signal?: AbortSignal;
}"""


LOOP_OLD = """  let attempt = 0;
  let lastResult: OrchestratorResult = { reason: 'crash' };

  const deadlineAt = opts.taskStartedAt + opts.totalTimeoutMs;

  while (true) {
    const remainingMs = deadlineAt - Date.now();

    if (remainingMs < opts.minRemainingMs) {
      opts.log('retry_abort', {
        reason: 'time_budget_exhausted',
        remaining_ms: remainingMs,
        attempt
      });
      break;
    }

    lastResult = await opts.runOnce(deadlineAt);

    if (!opts.isRetryable(lastResult.reason)) {
      break;
    }

    if (attempt >= opts.maxRetries) {
      opts.log('retry_abort', {
        reason: 'max_retries',
        attempt,
        max: opts.maxRetries
      });
      break;
    }

    attempt++;
    const waitMs =
      opts.backoffMs[attempt - 1] ??
      opts.backoffMs[opts.backoffMs.length - 1];

    opts.log('retry_scheduled', {
      attempt,
      max: opts.maxRetries,
      wait_ms: waitMs,
      reason: lastResult.reason
    });

    await opts.onRetry(attempt, opts.maxRetries, lastResult.reason);
    await sleep(waitMs);
  }

  return lastResult;
}"""

LOOP_NEW = """  let attempt = 0;
  let lastResult: OrchestratorResult = { reason: 'crash' };

  const deadlineAt = opts.taskStartedAt + opts.totalTimeoutMs;

  while (true) {
    if (opts.signal?.aborted) {
      opts.log('retry_abort', { reason: 'user_stopped', attempt });
      break;
    }

    const remainingMs = deadlineAt - Date.now();

    if (remainingMs < opts.minRemainingMs) {
      opts.log('retry_abort', {
        reason: 'time_budget_exhausted',
        remaining_ms: remainingMs,
        attempt
      });
      break;
    }

    lastResult = await opts.runOnce(deadlineAt);

    // Even if the attempt just finished, prefer reporting
    // user_stopped over the underlying reason: the user asked to
    // stop, and the next block would have sent the request anyway.
    if (opts.signal?.aborted) {
      opts.log('retry_abort', { reason: 'user_stopped', attempt });
      break;
    }

    if (!opts.isRetryable(lastResult.reason)) {
      break;
    }

    if (attempt >= opts.maxRetries) {
      opts.log('retry_abort', {
        reason: 'max_retries',
        attempt,
        max: opts.maxRetries
      });
      break;
    }

    attempt++;
    const waitMs =
      opts.backoffMs[attempt - 1] ??
      opts.backoffMs[opts.backoffMs.length - 1];

    opts.log('retry_scheduled', {
      attempt,
      max: opts.maxRetries,
      wait_ms: waitMs,
      reason: lastResult.reason
    });

    await opts.onRetry(attempt, opts.maxRetries, lastResult.reason);

    if (opts.signal?.aborted) {
      opts.log('retry_abort', { reason: 'user_stopped', attempt });
      break;
    }

    await sleepWithAbort(waitMs, opts.signal);
  }

  return lastResult;
}"""

- **Stop button aborts the retry loop.** Previously Stop only stopped
  the current Orchestrator; if the Orchestrator had already returned

async function t4_abort_during_backoff(): Promise<void> {
  console.log('\nT4: abort during backoff → loop exits promptly');

  const controller = new AbortController();
  let calls = 0;

  // Long backoff (10s) but we abort after 20ms. If abort works,
  // the loop finishes well before the backoff would have.
  const started = Date.now();
  const resultPromise = runWithRetry({
    taskStartedAt: Date.now(),
    totalTimeoutMs: 60_000,
    maxRetries: 3,
    backoffMs: [10_000, 10_000, 10_000],
    minRemainingMs: 100,
    signal: controller.signal,
    isRetryable: (r) => r === 'network_error',
    runOnce: async () => {
      calls++;
      return { reason: 'network_error' };
    },
    onRetry: async () => { /* no-op */ },
    log: () => { /* silent */ }
  });

  setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 20);
  const result = await resultPromise;
  const elapsed = Date.now() - started;

  check(calls === 1, `runOnce called once (got ${calls})`);
  check(elapsed < 1000,
    `finished in ${elapsed}ms (well under the 10s backoff)`);
  check(result.reason === 'network_error',
    `result.reason = ${result.reason} (last attempt)`);
}

async function main(): Promise<void> {
  t1_decision_table();
  await t2_onRetry_receives_reason();
  await t3_abort_before_first_attempt();
  await t4_abort_during_backoff();

  console.log();
  if (failures === 0) {
    console.log('=== SUCCESS: retry restart decision works ===');
    process.exit(0);
  } else {
    console.log(`=== FAILURE: ${failures} check(s) failed ===`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
}'''

===== FILE: scripts/dev/apply_step65_fallback_all_stops.py =====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Step 65: fallback summary on any stop reason.

Step 56 extended the fallback-summary condition to include 'timeout'.
A live ASDI run (runs5) surfaced the next gap: the task stopped with
network_error after a mid-request ECONNRESET, and no summary.md was
written — the condition still listed only done / deadlock / gave_up /
timeout.

Rather than chase reasons one by one, this step inverts the condition:
the fallback is written whenever summary.md does not exist, regardless
of how the task ended. The Critic's own summary is never overwritten.
Whatever ended the task — done, timeout, network_error, user_stopped,
protocol_violation, context_exhausted, crash — the user still needs
a persistent record of what happened.

One-line logical change. New probe covers two reasons that were not in
the old list (network_error, unknown_tool).

Run from the pingis/ extension root:
    python scripts/dev/apply_step65_fallback_all_stops.py
"""

import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
BACKUP = ROOT / ".backup" / "dev-snapshot-v35"


def backup(rel: str) -> None:
    src = ROOT / rel
    if not src.exists():
        return
    dst = BACKUP / rel
    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copy2(src, dst)


def patch(rel: str, pairs: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> int:
    p = ROOT / rel
    if not p.exists():
        print(f"  ✗ {rel}: not found")
        return -1
    text = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    original = text
    total = 0
    for old, new in pairs:
        if old == new:
            continue
        if new in text and old not in text:
            print(f"  = {rel}: already patched")
            continue
        if new in text and old in text:
            print(f"  ✗ {rel}: both old and new present — file drifted")
            return -1
        n = text.count(old)
        if n == 0:
            print(f"  ✗ {rel}: pattern not found; expected:")
            print(f"    {old[:200]!r}")
            return -1
        if n > 1:
            print(f"  ✗ {rel}: pattern appears {n} times; aborting")
            return -1
        text = text.replace(old, new)
        total += n
        print(f"  + {rel}: {n} occurrence(s)")
    if text != original:
        backup(rel)
        p.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    return total


def write_new(rel: str, content: str) -> None:
    p = ROOT / rel
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if p.exists():
        backup(rel)
    p.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"  + {rel} (new, {len(content)} bytes)")


def run_cmd(cmd: list[str], label: str) -> bool:
    print()
    print(f"=== {label} ===")
    print("$ " + " ".join(cmd))
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=ROOT)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print(f"  ✗ {label} failed (exit {r.returncode})")
        return False
    print(f"  + {label} ok")
    return True


def git_commit(message: str) -> None:
    if not (ROOT / ".git").exists():
        print("  git: no repo, skipping commit")
        return
    try:
        subprocess.run(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=ROOT,
                       check=True, capture_output=True)
        subprocess.run(["git", "commit", "-m", message], cwd=ROOT,
                       check=True, capture_output=True)
        print(f"  git: committed \"{message}\"")
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
        print(f"  git: commit failed ({e})")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# src/orchestrator.ts — invert the condition
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

COND_OLD = """      // Fallback summary when the Critic did not write one.
      // Covers clean done, deadlock (empty queues), and gave_up
      // (IMPOSSIBLE from an agent). All three end the task without
      // the Critic having written a summary; the user still needs a
      // persistent record of what happened.
      if ((this.stopReason === 'done' ||
           this.stopReason === 'deadlock' ||
           this.stopReason === 'gave_up' ||
           this.stopReason === 'timeout')
          && !fs.existsSync(summaryPath)) {
        this.writeFallbackSummary(summaryPath, planPath);
      }"""

COND_NEW = """      // Fallback summary when the Critic did not write one.
      // Unconditional on stop reason: whatever ended the task —
      // done, timeout, network_error, user_stopped,
      // protocol_violation, context_exhausted, crash — the user
      // still needs a persistent record. The only condition is that
      // the Critic has not written a summary itself; when it has,
      // that file is left untouched.
      if (!fs.existsSync(summaryPath)) {
        this.writeFallbackSummary(summaryPath, planPath);
      }"""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CHANGELOG
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

CHANGELOG_OLD = """## [Unreleased]"""

CHANGELOG_NEW = """## [Unreleased]

### Fixed

- **Fallback summary on any stop reason.** Previously `summary.md`
  was written only for `done`, `deadlock`, `gave_up`, and `timeout`.
  A live run stopped with `network_error` and left the user without
  a report. Now the orchestrator writes a fallback summary whenever
  the Critic did not, regardless of the stop reason. The Critic's
  own summary is never overwritten."""

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

PROBE = r'''/**
 * Unit test for step 65 — fallback summary on any stop reason.
 *
 * T1. network_error (StopError raised from api.chat) → summary.md
 *     written even though network_error is not in the "usual" list.
 * T2. unknown_tool (executor tries to call finalize) → summary.md
 *     written.
 * T3. The Critic's own summary is never overwritten: a fake Critic
 *     writes summary.md before finalize; orchestrator must not touch
 *     it.
 *
 * Run:
 *   npx ts-node --project scripts/tsconfig.json scripts/probe-fallback-summary.ts
 */

import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as os from 'os';
import * as path from 'path';
import { ApiClient } from '../src/api';
import { Executor } from '../src/executor';
import { Logger } from '../src/log';
import { NullPanel, Orchestrator } from '../src/orchestrator';
import { AssistantResponse, ExecResult, StopError } from '../src/types';

let failures = 0;

function check(condition: boolean, label: string): void {
  if (condition) {
    console.log(`  ✓ ${label}`);
  } else {
    console.error(`  ✗ ${label}`);
    failures++;
  }
}

function freshTmp(name: string): string {
  const p = path.join(os.tmpdir(),
    `${name}-${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8)}`);
  fs.mkdirSync(p, { recursive: true });
  return p;
}

type Step =
  | { kind: 'throw_stop'; reason: string }
  | { kind: 'tools'; calls: { name: string; args: any }[] };

class FakeApi {
  constructor(private who: string, private script: Step[]) {}
  private idx = 0;
  async newChat(): Promise<void> { /* no-op */ }
  async chat(): Promise<AssistantResponse> {
    if (this.idx >= this.script.length) {
      throw new Error(`FakeApi(${this.who}): script exhausted`);
    }
    const s = this.script[this.idx++];
    if (s.kind === 'throw_stop') {
      throw new StopError(s.reason as any, 'simulated');
    }
    return {
      text: '',
      tool_calls: s.calls.map((c, i) => ({
        id: `call_${this.idx}_${i}`,
        name: c.name as any,
        args: c.args
      })) as any,
      raw: {}
    };
  }
}

class FakeExecutor {
  async run(call_id: string, script: string): Promise<ExecResult> {
    return {
      call_id, command: 'noop', exit_code: 0, duration_ms: 1,
      stdout: 'ok\n', stderr: '',
      stdout_truncated: false, stderr_truncated: false
    };
  }
}

function mkLog(cwd: string): Logger {
  return new Logger(cwd, { appendLine: () => { /* silent */ } });
}

async function runOrch(
  cwd: string,
  apiE: FakeApi,
  apiC: FakeApi
): Promise<void> {
  const log = mkLog(cwd);
  const orch = new Orchestrator(
    apiE as unknown as ApiClient,
    apiC as unknown as ApiClient,
    new FakeExecutor() as unknown as Executor,
    new NullPanel(),
    log,
    {
      cwd, name: 'probe-fallback-summary', task: 'stub',
      deadlineAt: Date.now() + 30_000,
      executorPrompt: 'E', criticPrompt: 'C'
    }
  );
  await orch.run();
  log.close();
  await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 200));
}

function readLog(cwd: string): any[] {
  const logPath = path.join(cwd, '.pingis', 'session.log');
  if (!fs.existsSync(logPath)) return [];
  return fs.readFileSync(logPath, 'utf-8')
    .split('\n').filter(Boolean).map(l => JSON.parse(l));
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async function t1_network_error(): Promise<void> {
  console.log('\nT1: network_error → summary written');

  const cwd = freshTmp('probe-fallback-t1');
  fs.mkdirSync(path.join(cwd, '.pingis'), { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(cwd, '.pingis', 'plan.md'),
    '# Plan\nreal content\n');

  const apiE = new FakeApi('executor', [
    { kind: 'throw_stop', reason: 'network_error' }
  ]);
  const apiC = new FakeApi('critic', []);

  await runOrch(cwd, apiE, apiC);
  const lines = readLog(cwd);

  const stop = lines.find(e => e.event === 'stop');
  const summary = path.join(cwd, '.pingis', 'summary.md');
  const plan = path.join(cwd, '.pingis', 'plan.md');

  check(stop?.reason === 'network_error',
    `stop reason = ${stop?.reason} (expected network_error)`);
  check(fs.existsSync(summary),
    'summary.md written even for network_error');
  check(fs.existsSync(plan),
    'plan.md preserved (graceful shutdown keeps it)');
}

async function t2_unknown_tool(): Promise<void> {
  console.log('\nT2: unknown_tool (executor calls finalize) → summary written');

  const cwd = freshTmp('probe-fallback-t2');
  fs.mkdirSync(path.join(cwd, '.pingis'), { recursive: true });

  const apiE = new FakeApi('executor', [
    { kind: 'tools',
      calls: [{ name: 'finalize', args: { comment: 'not mine' } }] }
  ]);
  const apiC = new FakeApi('critic', []);

  await runOrch(cwd, apiE, apiC);
  const lines = readLog(cwd);

  const stop = lines.find(e => e.event === 'stop');
  const summary = path.join(cwd, '.pingis', 'summary.md');

  check(stop?.reason === 'unknown_tool',
    `stop reason = ${stop?.reason} (expected unknown_tool)`);
  check(fs.existsSync(summary),
    'summary.md written even for unknown_tool');
}

async function t3_critic_summary_untouched(): Promise<void> {
  console.log('\nT3: Critic writes its own summary → orchestrator leaves it');

  const cwd = freshTmp('probe-fallback-t3');
  fs.mkdirSync(path.join(cwd, '.pingis'), { recursive: true });

  // Executor: ALL DONE. Critic: execute (to write summary), finalize.
  // The FakeExecutor is stubbed — it does not actually write a file.
  // So we create summary.md up front to simulate the Critic having
  // written it before finalize.
  const summary = path.join(cwd, '.pingis', 'summary.md');
  fs.writeFileSync(summary,
    '# Task summary\n\nCritic-authored content. Do not touch.\n');

  const apiE = new FakeApi('executor', [
    { kind: 'tools',
      calls: [{ name: 'send_message',
                args: { to: 'critic', message: 'ALL DONE: ok' } }] }
  ]);
  const apiC = new FakeApi('critic', [
    { kind: 'tools',
      calls: [{ name: 'finalize', args: { comment: 'done' } }] }
  ]);

  await runOrch(cwd, apiE, apiC);

  const text = fs.readFileSync(summary, 'utf-8');
  check(text.includes('Critic-authored content'),
    'critic summary not overwritten');
  check(!text.includes('fallback'),
    'fallback marker absent');
}

async function main(): Promise<void> {
  await t1_network_error();
  await t2_unknown_tool();
  await t3_critic_summary_untouched();

  console.log();
  if (failures === 0) {
    console.log('=== SUCCESS: fallback summary on any stop ===');
    process.exit(0);

    console.log(`=== FAILURE: ${failures} check(s) failed ===`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
}

main().catch(e => {
  console.error('CRASH:', e);
  process.exit(2);
});

def patch_package_json() -> None:
    p = ROOT / "package.json"
    if not p.exists():
        print("  ✗ package.json not found")
        return
    backup("package.json")
    data = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    scripts = data["scripts"]
    scripts["probe:fallback-summary"] = (
        "ts-node --project scripts/tsconfig.json scripts/probe-fallback-summary.ts"
    )
    order = ["compile", "watch", "typecheck:scripts", "vscode:prepublish",
             "probe:409", "probe:help", "probe:help-protocol",
             "probe:exec", "probe:artifacts", "probe:retry", "probe:phase",
             "probe:return-to-original", "probe:format-budget",
             "probe:context-transition", "probe:soft-deadline",
             "probe:checkpoint-nudge", "probe:continuation-nudge",
             "probe:plan-markers", "probe:retry-restart",
             "probe:fallback-summary"]
    ordered: dict[str, str] = {}
    for k in order:
        if k in scripts:
            ordered[k] = scripts.pop(k)
    ordered.update(scripts)
    data["scripts"] = ordered
    p.write_text(
        json.dumps(data, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    print("  + package.json: added probe:fallback-summary")

===== FILE: scripts/dev/apply_step66_reset_stale_summary.py =====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Step 66: clear stale summary.md at the start of a new task.

runs6 exposed a latent problem: summary.md is the report of the LAST
task. When a new task starts in a folder where a summary already
exists, the fallback writer (added in step65) sees the file and skips
its own write — fs.existsSync is true. Result: if the Critic fails to
write its own summary, the user is left with a report about the
PREVIOUS task, not the current one.

Fix: at the start of Orchestrator.run(), unlink summary.md if it
exists. Same treatment plan.md gets from the artifact lifecycle:
state from a previous task must not survive into the next.

Kept the operation logged as
`event: 'artifact', action: 'reset', kind: 'summary'`.

Run from the pingis/ extension root:
    python scripts/dev/apply_step66_reset_stale_summary.py
"""

import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
BACKUP = ROOT / ".backup" / "dev-snapshot-v36"


def backup(rel: str) -> None:
    src = ROOT / rel
    if not src.exists():
        return
    dst = BACKUP / rel
    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copy2(src, dst)


def patch(rel: str, pairs: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> int:
    p = ROOT / rel
    if not p.exists():
        print(f"  ✗ {rel}: not found")
        return -1
    text = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    original = text
    total = 0
    for old, new in pairs:
        if old == new:
            continue
        if new in text and old not in text:
            print(f"  = {rel}: already patched")
            continue
        if new in text and old in text:
            print(f"  ✗ {rel}: both old and new present — file drifted")
            return -1
        n = text.count(old)
        if n == 0:
            print(f"  ✗ {rel}: pattern not found; expected:")
            print(f"    {old[:200]!r}")
            return -1
        if n > 1:
            print(f"  ✗ {rel}: pattern appears {n} times; aborting")
            return -1
        text = text.replace(old, new)
        total += n
        print(f"  + {rel}: {n} occurrence(s)")
    if text != original:
        backup(rel)
        p.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    return total


def run_cmd(cmd: list[str], label: str) -> bool:
    print()
    print(f"=== {label} ===")
    print("$ " + " ".join(cmd))
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=ROOT)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print(f"  ✗ {label} failed (exit {r.returncode})")
        return False
    print(f"  + {label} ok")
    return True


def git_commit(message: str) -> None:
    if not (ROOT / ".git").exists():
        print("  git: no repo, skipping commit")
        return
    try:
        subprocess.run(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=ROOT,
                       check=True, capture_output=True)
        subprocess.run(["git", "commit", "-m", message], cwd=ROOT,
                       check=True, capture_output=True)
        print(f"  git: committed \"{message}\"")
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
        print(f"  git: commit failed ({e})")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# src/orchestrator.ts — reset stale summary.md
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

ANCHOR_OLD = """    } else {
      this.log.event('orchestrator', 'artifact', {
        action: 'resume',
        kind: 'chats',
        reason: 'plan.md present and project matches',
        path: planPath
      });
    }

    this.queueE.push({"""

ANCHOR_NEW = """    } else {
      this.log.event('orchestrator', 'artifact', {
        action: 'resume',
        kind: 'chats',
        reason: 'plan.md present and project matches',
        path: planPath
      });
    }

    // Clear stale summary.md from a previous task. Like plan.md,
    // summary.md is state for THIS task, not the previous one.
    // Leaving it in place would make the fallback writer a no-op
    // (it checks !fs.existsSync) and would show the user a report
    // about a different task.
    const staleSummary = path.join(this.opts.cwd, '.pingis', 'summary.md');
    if (fs.existsSync(staleSummary)) {
      try {
        fs.unlinkSync(staleSummary);
        this.log.event('orchestrator', 'artifact', {
          action: 'reset',
          kind: 'summary',
          reason: 'new task',
          path: staleSummary
        });
      } catch (e) {
        this.log.event('orchestrator', 'error', {
          stage: 'summary_reset',
          code: 'unlink_failed',
          detail: String(e)
        });
      }
    }

    this.queueE.push({"""

===== FILE: scripts/dev/apply_step66a_fix_probe_t3.py =====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Step 66a: fix T3 in probe-fallback-summary after step66.

Step66 clears summary.md at task start. The old T3 pre-populated
summary.md before running the orchestrator and expected it to
survive — a pattern that step66 intentionally breaks. T3 now fails.

Fix: T3 simulates the Critic writing summary.md *during* the run —
via an execute call — which matches real behavior. FakeExecutor
gains a cwd and writes summary.md when the script mentions it,
same pattern as probe-artifacts.ts.

Commits step66 (on disk, uncommitted) together with 66a.

Run from the pingis/ extension root:
    python scripts/dev/apply_step66a_fix_probe_t3.py
"""

import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
BACKUP = ROOT / ".backup" / "dev-snapshot-v36"


def backup(rel: str) -> None:
    src = ROOT / rel
    if not src.exists():
        return
    dst = BACKUP / rel
    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copy2(src, dst)


def patch(rel: str, pairs: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> int:
    p = ROOT / rel
    if not p.exists():
        print(f"  ✗ {rel}: not found")
        return -1
    text = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    original = text
    total = 0
    for old, new in pairs:
        if old == new:
            continue
        if new in text and old not in text:
            print(f"  = {rel}: already patched")
            continue
        if new in text and old in text:
            print(f"  ✗ {rel}: both old and new present — file drifted")
            return -1
        n = text.count(old)
        if n == 0:
            print(f"  ✗ {rel}: pattern not found; expected:")
            print(f"    {old[:200]!r}")
            return -1
        if n > 1:
            print(f"  ✗ {rel}: pattern appears {n} times; aborting")
            return -1
        text = text.replace(old, new)
        total += n
        print(f"  + {rel}: {n} occurrence(s)")
    if text != original:
        backup(rel)
        p.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    return total


def run_cmd(cmd: list[str], label: str) -> bool:
    print()
    print(f"=== {label} ===")
    print("$ " + " ".join(cmd))
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=ROOT)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print(f"  ✗ {label} failed (exit {r.returncode})")
        return False
    print(f"  + {label} ok")
    return True


def git_commit(message: str) -> None:
    if not (ROOT / ".git").exists():
        print("  git: no repo, skipping commit")
        return
    try:
        subprocess.run(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=ROOT,
                       check=True, capture_output=True)
        subprocess.run(["git", "commit", "-m", message], cwd=ROOT,
                       check=True, capture_output=True)
        print(f"  git: committed \"{message}\"")
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
        print(f"  git: commit failed ({e})")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Patch 1 — FakeExecutor writes summary.md when script mentions it
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

EXEC_OLD = """class FakeExecutor {
  async run(call_id: string, script: string): Promise<ExecResult> {
    return {
      call_id, command: 'noop', exit_code: 0, duration_ms: 1,
      stdout: 'ok\\n', stderr: '',
      stdout_truncated: false, stderr_truncated: false
    };
  }
}"""

EXEC_NEW = """class FakeExecutor {
  constructor(private cwd: string) {}

  async run(call_id: string, script: string): Promise<ExecResult> {
    // In real use, the Critic writes .pingis/summary.md via execute.
    // When the fake script mentions summary.md, simulate that write
    // so probes can verify the orchestrator leaves the file alone.
    if (script.includes('summary.md')) {
      const dir = path.join(this.cwd, '.pingis');
      fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
      fs.writeFileSync(
        path.join(dir, 'summary.md'),
        '# Task summary\\n\\nCritic-authored content. Do not touch.\\n'
      );
    }
    return {
      call_id, command: 'noop', exit_code: 0, duration_ms: 1,
      stdout: 'ok\\n', stderr: '',
      stdout_truncated: false, stderr_truncated: false
    };
  }
}"""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Patch 2 — runOrch passes cwd to FakeExecutor
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

CALL_OLD = """    new FakeExecutor() as unknown as Executor,"""

CALL_NEW = """    new FakeExecutor(cwd) as unknown as Executor,"""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Patch 3 — T3 rewritten to write summary via execute
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

T3_OLD = """async function t3_critic_summary_untouched(): Promise<void> {
  console.log('\\nT3: Critic writes its own summary → orchestrator leaves it');

  const cwd = freshTmp('probe-fallback-t3');

  // Executor: ALL DONE. Critic: execute (to write summary), finalize.
  // The FakeExecutor is stubbed — it does not actually write a file.

  const summary = path.join(cwd, '.pingis', 'summary.md');
  fs.writeFileSync(summary,
    '# Task summary\\n\\nCritic-authored content. Do not touch.\\n');

  const apiE = new FakeApi('executor', [
    { kind: 'tools',
      calls: [{ name: 'send_message',
                args: { to: 'critic', message: 'ALL DONE: ok' } }] }
  ]);
  const apiC = new FakeApi('critic', [
    { kind: 'tools',
      calls: [{ name: 'finalize', args: { comment: 'done' } }] }
  ]);

  await runOrch(cwd, apiE, apiC);

  const text = fs.readFileSync(summary, 'utf-8');
  check(text.includes('Critic-authored content'),
    'critic summary not overwritten');
  check(!text.includes('fallback'),
    'fallback marker absent');
}"""

T3_NEW = """async function t3_critic_summary_untouched(): Promise<void> {
  console.log('\\nT3: Critic writes its own summary → orchestrator leaves it');

  const apiC = new FakeApi('critic', [
    { kind: 'tools',
      calls: [{ name: 'execute',
                args: { script: 'print("write .pingis/summary.md")' } }] },
    { kind: 'tools',
      calls: [{ name: 'finalize', args: { comment: 'done' } }] }
  ]);

  await runOrch(cwd, apiE, apiC);

  const summary = path.join(cwd, '.pingis', 'summary.md');
  const text = fs.readFileSync(summary, 'utf-8');
  check(text.includes('Critic-authored content'),
    'critic summary not overwritten');
  check(!text.includes('fallback'),
    'fallback marker absent');
}"""


def main() -> int:
    if not (ROOT / "package.json").exists() or not (ROOT / "src").exists():
        print("ERROR: run from the pingis/ extension root.")

    BACKUP.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

===== FILE: scripts/dev/apply_step67_grace_and_time_limit.py =====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Step 67: 30-minute grace period + economical TIME_LIMIT handler.

Two changes to close the runs6 failure mode.

1. GRACE_MS raised from 300s to 1_800_000 (30 minutes). Live runs
   showed the Critic's first LLM turn after soft deadline can take
   89+ seconds, and completing the finalize flow requires 2-3 more.
   300s left no room for a slow DeepSeek Web. The task budget
   (taskTimeoutMinutes) still caps the run; only the window AFTER
   the soft deadline grows.

2. The TIME_LIMIT: handler in the Critic prompt is rewritten as a
   strict three-step sequence: one execute to gather context
   (plan.md + 2-3 recent logs, all in one script), one execute to
   write summary.md, one finalize. Previously it invited an open-
   ended investigation that cost several turns.

Run from the pingis/ extension root:
    python scripts/dev/apply_step67_grace_and_time_limit.py
"""

import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
BACKUP = ROOT / ".backup" / "dev-snapshot-v37"


def backup(rel: str) -> None:
    src = ROOT / rel
    if not src.exists():
        return
    dst = BACKUP / rel
    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copy2(src, dst)


def patch(rel: str, pairs: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> int:
    p = ROOT / rel
    if not p.exists():
        print(f"  ✗ {rel}: not found")
        return -1
    text = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    original = text
    total = 0
    for old, new in pairs:
        if old == new:
            continue
        if new in text and old not in text:
            print(f"  = {rel}: already patched")
            continue
        if new in text and old in text:
            print(f"  ✗ {rel}: both old and new present — file drifted")
            return -1
        n = text.count(old)
        if n == 0:
            print(f"  ✗ {rel}: pattern not found; expected:")
            print(f"    {old[:200]!r}")
            return -1
        if n > 1:
            print(f"  ✗ {rel}: pattern appears {n} times; aborting")
            return -1
        text = text.replace(old, new)
        total += n
        print(f"  + {rel}: {n} occurrence(s)")
    if text != original:
        backup(rel)
        p.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    return total


def write_new(rel: str, content: str) -> None:
    p = ROOT / rel
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if p.exists():
        backup(rel)
    p.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"  + {rel} (new, {len(content)} bytes)")


def run_cmd(cmd: list[str], label: str) -> bool:
    print()
    print(f"=== {label} ===")
    print("$ " + " ".join(cmd))
    r = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=ROOT)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print(f"  ✗ {label} failed (exit {r.returncode})")
        return False
    print(f"  + {label} ok")
    return True


def git_commit(message: str) -> None:
    if not (ROOT / ".git").exists():
        print("  git: no repo, skipping commit")
        return
    try:
        subprocess.run(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=ROOT,
                       check=True, capture_output=True)
        subprocess.run(["git", "commit", "-m", message], cwd=ROOT,
                       check=True, capture_output=True)
        print(f"  git: committed \"{message}\"")
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
        print(f"  git: commit failed ({e})")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# src/orchestrator.ts — GRACE_MS
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

GRACE_OLD = """/**
 * Extra time granted after the soft deadline so a graceful shutdown
 * (Critic finalizing, plan.md / summary.md written) can complete.
 * Added once, to the absolute deadline, not once per attempt.
 *
 * 300_000 (5 minutes) is calibrated against real runs: on a long
 * task the Critic's first LLM turn alone can take 55+ seconds, and
 * finalizing needs at least three turns — read plan.md, write
 * summary.md via execute, then call finalize. 120_000 left no room
 * for that; 300_000 does.
 *
 * Probes override this via OrchestratorOptions.graceMs; production
 * uses this default.
 */
const GRACE_MS = 300_000;"""

GRACE_NEW = """/**
 * Extra time granted after the soft deadline so a graceful shutdown
 * (Critic finalizing, plan.md / summary.md written) can complete.
 * Added once, to the absolute deadline, not once per attempt.
 *
 * 1_800_000 (30 minutes). Live runs6 showed the Critic's first LLM
 * turn after soft deadline can take 89+ seconds, and completing the
 * finalize flow requires 2-3 more turns. 300_000 left no room for a
 * slow DeepSeek Web response. 30 minutes covers 5-10 slow turns even
 * in the worst case.
 *
 * The task budget (taskTimeoutMinutes) still caps the total run;
 * only the graceful-shutdown window grows.
 *
 * Probes override this via OrchestratorOptions.graceMs; production
 * uses this default.
 */
const GRACE_MS = 1_800_000;"""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# src/prompts.ts — TIME_LIMIT handler in Critic prompt
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

TIME_LIMIT_OLD = """"TIME_LIMIT: ...":
  The overall task time has expired. Read .pingis/plan.md (if present)
  and key files. Assess what's done and what's not. Call finalize
  with an honest summary: what's done, what's not, what the user
  should do when restarting the task. Do not try to keep working —
  finalize immediately."""

TIME_LIMIT_NEW = """"TIME_LIMIT: ...":
  The overall task time has expired. Finalize in at most THREE turns.

  Turn 1 — one execute that gathers everything at once (do not split):
    • print .pingis/plan.md (if it exists),
    • list the contents of the runs/ directory (or whatever run
      directory the task used), newest first,
    • print the tail of the 2-3 most recent run logs.

  Turn 2 — one execute that writes .pingis/summary.md with:
    • Goal (from plan.md or the task),
    • Outcome (completed / stopped-incomplete / impossible),
    • Stages done / not done (copy the checkboxes from plan.md),
    • Files touched, verification performed, notes for resuming.

  Turn 3 — call finalize.

  Do NOT go deep. Do NOT re-read files you have already seen. A short
  honest summary beats a thorough one that misses the deadline. The
  goal is to leave the user a usable report, not to solve the task."""


def main() -> int:
    if not (ROOT / "package.json").exists() or not (ROOT / "src").exists():

    rc = patch("CHANGELOG.md", [(CHANGELOG_OLD, CHANGELOG_NEW)])
    if rc < 0:

    # Extend probe-plan-markers with a check for the TIME_LIMIT text.

    print("--- scripts/probe-plan-markers.ts ---")

===== FILE: scripts/probe-409.ts =====
/**
 * Unit test for 409 context_exhausted handling.
 *
 * Mocks ApiClient and Executor. No real API servers needed.
 * Checks:
 *   1. deadE = true after 409 on the Executor side.
 *   2. Critic receives CONTEXT_LIMIT and calls finalize.
 *   3. stop reason=done (not context_exhausted).
 *
 * Run:
 *   npx ts-node --project scripts/tsconfig.json scripts/probe-409.ts
 */

import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as os from 'os';
import * as path from 'path';
import { ApiClient } from '../src/api';
import { Executor } from '../src/executor';
import { Logger } from '../src/log';
import { NullPanel, Orchestrator } from '../src/orchestrator';
import { AssistantResponse, ExecResult, StopError } from '../src/types';

const TMP = path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'probe-409-' + Date.now());
fs.mkdirSync(TMP, { recursive: true });
console.log('TMP:', TMP);

const log = new Logger(TMP, {
  appendLine: (s: string) => console.log(s)
});

type Step = 'execute' | 'send_message' | 'finalize' | '409';

class FakeApi {
  private count = 0;
  constructor(
    private who: string,
    private script: Step[]
  ) {}

  async newChat(): Promise<void> {
    /* no-op */
  }

  async chat(): Promise<AssistantResponse> {
    const step = this.script[this.count++];
    console.log(`[fake-${this.who}] step #${this.count}: ${step}`);

    if (step === '409') {
      throw new StopError('context_exhausted', `fake ${this.who}`);
    }

    if (step === 'execute') {
      return {
        text: '',
        tool_calls: [{
          id: `call_${this.count}`,
          name: 'execute',
          args: { script: 'print("noop")' }
        } as any],
        raw: {}
      };
    }

    if (step === 'send_message') {
      return {
        text: '',
        tool_calls: [{
          id: `call_${this.count}`,
          name: 'send_message',
          args: this.who === 'executor'
            ? { to: 'critic', message: 'STAGE 1/1 DONE: done' }
            : { to: 'executor', message: 'APPROVE_STAGE' }
        } as any],
        raw: {}
      };
    }

    if (step === 'finalize') {
      return {
        text: '',
        tool_calls: [{
          id: `call_${this.count}`,
          name: 'finalize',
          args: { comment: 'Executor context exhausted. Saved 1/1.' }
        } as any],
        raw: {}
      };
    }

    throw new Error('unknown step: ' + step);
  }
}

class FakeExecutor {
  async run(call_id: string, script: string, command?: string): Promise<ExecResult> {
    console.log(`[fake-exec] script len=${script.length}`);
    return {
      call_id,
      command: command ?? 'noop',
      exit_code: 0,
      duration_ms: 1,
      stdout: 'noop\n',
      stderr: '',
      stdout_truncated: false,
      stderr_truncated: false
    };
  }
}

// E: execute -> send_message -> 409
// C: send_message (APPROVE_STAGE) -> finalize
const fakeApiE = new FakeApi('executor', ['execute', 'send_message', '409']);
const fakeApiC = new FakeApi('critic', ['send_message', 'finalize']);

async function readLogWhenReady(logPath: string, timeoutMs = 3000): Promise<string> {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
    if (fs.existsSync(logPath)) {
      const text = fs.readFileSync(logPath, 'utf-8');
      if (text.includes('"event":"stop"')) return text;
    }
    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 50));
  }
  return fs.existsSync(logPath) ? fs.readFileSync(logPath, 'utf-8') : '';
}

async function main() {
  const orch = new Orchestrator(
    fakeApiE as unknown as ApiClient,
    fakeApiC as unknown as ApiClient,
    new FakeExecutor() as unknown as Executor,
    new NullPanel(),
    log,
    {
      cwd: TMP,
      name: 'probe-409',
      task: 'Stub task for 409 handling test.',
      deadlineAt: Date.now() + 60_000,
      executorPrompt: 'EXECUTOR_PROMPT',
      criticPrompt: 'CRITIC_PROMPT'
    }
  );

  await orch.run();
  log.close();

  const logPath = path.join(TMP, '.pingis', 'session.log');
  const logText = await readLogWhenReady(logPath);
  const lines = logText
    .split('\n')
    .filter(Boolean)
    .map(l => JSON.parse(l));

  const stopEvent = lines.find(e => e.event === 'stop');
  const exhaustedEvent = lines.find(
    e => e.event === 'error' && e.code === 'executor_exhausted'
  );
  const criticFinalize = lines.find(
    e => e.who === 'critic'
      && e.event === 'response'
      && Array.isArray(e.tool_calls)
      && (e.tool_calls as any[]).some(tc => tc?.name === 'finalize')
  );

  console.log();
  console.log('--- CHECKS ---');
  console.log('executor_exhausted event:', !!exhaustedEvent);
  console.log('critic finalized:', !!criticFinalize);
  console.log('stop reason:', stopEvent?.reason);

  let failures = 0;
  if (!exhaustedEvent) {
    console.error('FAIL: no executor_exhausted event');
    failures++;
  }
  if (!criticFinalize) {
    console.error("FAIL: Critic did not finalize (didn't receive CONTEXT_LIMIT?)");
    failures++;
  }
  if (!stopEvent || stopEvent.reason !== 'done') {
    console.error(`FAIL: stop reason = ${stopEvent?.reason}, expected done`);
    failures++;
  }

  if (failures === 0) {
    console.log();
    console.log('=== SUCCESS: 409 per-agent handled correctly ===');
    process.exit(0);
  } else {
    console.log();
    console.log(`=== FAILURE: ${failures} checks failed ===`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
}

main().catch(e => {
  console.error('CRASH:', e);
  process.exit(2);
});
===== END FILE: scripts/probe-409.ts =====

===== FILE: scripts/probe-artifacts.ts =====
/**
 * Unit test for step 31 — artifact lifecycle and chat reset.
 *
 * Mocks ApiClient and Executor. No real API servers needed.
 *
 * Scenarios:
 *   T1. No .pingis/plan.md -> newChat() called for both agents.
 *   T2. .pingis/plan.md present -> newChat() not called.
 *   T3. Done without Critic writing summary.md -> orchestrator writes
 *       a fallback summary; plan.md removed (clean done).
 *   T4. Done with Critic writing summary.md -> orchestrator does not
 *       overwrite; plan.md removed (clean done).
 *
 * Run:
 *   npx ts-node --project scripts/tsconfig.json scripts/probe-artifacts.ts
 */

import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as os from 'os';
import * as path from 'path';
import { ApiClient } from '../src/api';
import { Executor } from '../src/executor';
import { Logger } from '../src/log';
import { NullPanel, Orchestrator } from '../src/orchestrator';
import { AssistantResponse, ExecResult, StopError } from '../src/types';

let failures = 0;

function check(condition: boolean, label: string): void {
  if (condition) {
    console.log(`  ✓ ${label}`);
  } else {
    console.error(`  ✗ ${label}`);
    failures++;
  }
}

function freshTmp(name: string): string {
  const p = path.join(os.tmpdir(), `${name}-${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8)}`);
  fs.mkdirSync(p, { recursive: true });
  return p;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Fake APIs
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class FakeApiImmediateExhaust {
  public newChatCalls = 0;
  async newChat(): Promise<void> { this.newChatCalls++; }
  async chat(): Promise<AssistantResponse> {
    throw new StopError('context_exhausted', 'fake');
  }
}

class FakeApiStepScript {
  private step = 0;
  constructor(private who: 'executor' | 'critic', private writeSummary: boolean) {}
  public newChatCalls = 0;
  async newChat(): Promise<void> { this.newChatCalls++; }
  async chat(): Promise<AssistantResponse> {
    this.step++;
    const mk = (name: any, args: any): AssistantResponse => ({
      text: '',
      tool_calls: [{ id: `call_${this.step}`, name, args } as any],
      raw: {}
    });
    if (this.who === 'executor') {
      if (this.step === 1) return mk('execute', { script: 'print("noop")' });
      if (this.step === 2) return mk('send_message', { to: 'critic', message: 'ALL DONE: finished' });
    } else {
      if (this.step === 1) {
        const script = this.writeSummary
          ? 'pathlib.Path(".pingis/summary.md").write_text("MARKER", encoding="utf-8")'
          : 'print("noop")';
        return mk('execute', { script });
      }
      if (this.step === 2) return mk('finalize', { comment: 'done' });
    }
    throw new Error(`exhausted: ${this.who} step ${this.step}`);
  }
}

class FakeExecutor {
  constructor(private cwd: string) {}
  async run(call_id: string, script: string): Promise<ExecResult> {
    if (script.includes('summary.md')) {
      const dir = path.join(this.cwd, '.pingis');
      fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
      fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, 'summary.md'), '# Task summary\n\nMarker written by fake executor.\n');
    }
    return {
      call_id,
      command: 'noop',
      exit_code: 0,
      duration_ms: 1,
      stdout: 'ok\n',
      stderr: '',
      stdout_truncated: false,
      stderr_truncated: false
    };
  }
}

function makeLog(cwd: string): Logger {
  return new Logger(cwd, { appendLine: () => { /* silent */ } });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// T1 / T2 — chat reset decision
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async function t1_noPlan_resetsChats(): Promise<void> {
  console.log('\nT1: no plan.md -> newChat() called for both agents');
  const cwd = freshTmp('probe-artifacts-t1');
  const apiE = new FakeApiImmediateExhaust();
  const apiC = new FakeApiImmediateExhaust();
  const log = makeLog(cwd);

  const orch = new Orchestrator(
    apiE as unknown as ApiClient,
    apiC as unknown as ApiClient,
    new FakeExecutor(cwd) as unknown as Executor,
    new NullPanel(),
    log,
    {
      cwd, name: 't1', task: 'stub',
      deadlineAt: Date.now() + 10_000,
      executorPrompt: 'E', criticPrompt: 'C'
    }
  );

  await orch.run();
  log.close();

  check(apiE.newChatCalls === 1, `executor newChat called once (got ${apiE.newChatCalls})`);
  check(apiC.newChatCalls === 1, `critic newChat called once (got ${apiC.newChatCalls})`);
}

async function t2_withPlan_doesNotReset(): Promise<void> {
  console.log('\nT2: plan.md present -> newChat() not called');
  const cwd = freshTmp('probe-artifacts-t2');
  fs.mkdirSync(path.join(cwd, '.pingis'), { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(cwd, '.pingis', 'plan.md'), '# Plan\n');

  const apiE = new FakeApiImmediateExhaust();
  const apiC = new FakeApiImmediateExhaust();
  const log = makeLog(cwd);

  const orch = new Orchestrator(
    apiE as unknown as ApiClient,
    apiC as unknown as ApiClient,
    new FakeExecutor(cwd) as unknown as Executor,
    new NullPanel(),
    log,
    {
      cwd, name: 't2', task: 'stub',
      deadlineAt: Date.now() + 10_000,
      executorPrompt: 'E', criticPrompt: 'C'
    }
  );

  await orch.run();
  log.close();

  check(apiE.newChatCalls === 0, `executor newChat not called (got ${apiE.newChatCalls})`);
  check(apiC.newChatCalls === 0, `critic newChat not called (got ${apiC.newChatCalls})`);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// T3 / T4 — summary and plan lifecycle
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async function t3_doneWithoutSummary_writesFallback(): Promise<void> {
  console.log('\nT3: done without Critic summary -> fallback written; plan deleted');
  const cwd = freshTmp('probe-artifacts-t3');
  fs.mkdirSync(path.join(cwd, '.pingis'), { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(cwd, '.pingis', 'plan.md'), '# Plan\nOriginal plan content.\n');

  const apiE = new FakeApiStepScript('executor', false);
  const apiC = new FakeApiStepScript('critic', false);
  const log = makeLog(cwd);

  const orch = new Orchestrator(
    apiE as unknown as ApiClient,
    apiC as unknown as ApiClient,
    new FakeExecutor(cwd) as unknown as Executor,
    new NullPanel(),
    log,
    {
      cwd, name: 't3', task: 'stub task',
      deadlineAt: Date.now() + 30_000,
      executorPrompt: 'E', criticPrompt: 'C'
    }
  );

  await orch.run();
  log.close();

  const summaryPath = path.join(cwd, '.pingis', 'summary.md');
  const planPath = path.join(cwd, '.pingis', 'plan.md');
  check(fs.existsSync(summaryPath), 'summary.md created');
  if (fs.existsSync(summaryPath)) {
    const text = fs.readFileSync(summaryPath, 'utf-8');
    check(text.includes('fallback'), 'summary contains fallback marker');
    check(text.includes('Original plan content'), 'summary contains plan verbatim');
  }
  check(!fs.existsSync(planPath), 'plan.md deleted on clean done');
}

async function t4_doneWithSummary_keepsCriticVersion(): Promise<void> {
  console.log('\nT4: done with Critic summary -> not overwritten; plan deleted');
  const cwd = freshTmp('probe-artifacts-t4');
  fs.mkdirSync(path.join(cwd, '.pingis'), { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(cwd, '.pingis', 'plan.md'), '# Plan\n');

  const apiE = new FakeApiStepScript('executor', false);
  const apiC = new FakeApiStepScript('critic', true);
  const log = makeLog(cwd);

  const orch = new Orchestrator(
    apiE as unknown as ApiClient,
    apiC as unknown as ApiClient,
    new FakeExecutor(cwd) as unknown as Executor,
    new NullPanel(),
    log,
    {
      cwd, name: 't4', task: 'stub task',
      deadlineAt: Date.now() + 30_000,
      executorPrompt: 'E', criticPrompt: 'C'
    }
  );

  await orch.run();
  log.close();

  const summaryPath = path.join(cwd, '.pingis', 'summary.md');
  const planPath = path.join(cwd, '.pingis', 'plan.md');
  check(fs.existsSync(summaryPath), 'summary.md exists');
  if (fs.existsSync(summaryPath)) {
    const text = fs.readFileSync(summaryPath, 'utf-8');
    check(text.includes('Marker written by fake executor'), 'summary left untouched by orchestrator');
    check(!text.includes('fallback'), 'fallback marker absent');
  }
  check(!fs.existsSync(planPath), 'plan.md deleted on clean done');
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Entry
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async function main(): Promise<void> {
  await t1_noPlan_resetsChats();
  await t2_withPlan_doesNotReset();
  await t3_doneWithoutSummary_writesFallback();
  await t4_doneWithSummary_keepsCriticVersion();

  console.log();
  if (failures === 0) {
    console.log('=== SUCCESS: artifact lifecycle works ===');
    process.exit(0);
  } else {
    console.log(`=== FAILURE: ${failures} check(s) failed ===`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
}

main().catch(e => {
  console.error('CRASH:', e);
  process.exit(2);
});
